chunks: And when your Lord proclaimed: "If you are grateful, I will surely increase you; but if you are thankless, then surely My punishment is very great."
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between gratitude and divine increase in Islam?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the concept of 'increase' (ziyadah) not merely in material wealth but in spiritual insight and proximity to the Divine, reflecting the Imams' role as guides of gratitude. The conditional structure emphasizes human agency, where the preservation and enhancement of divine favors depend on conscious recognition (shukr) versus neglect or denial (kufr). This dynamic underscores the Shia understanding of the covenant between God and humanity, where gratitude is an active state of being rather than passive acknowledgment.
